article.title: Why Capacity Planning Should Include Review Work
article.why: 把 review capacity 納入 AI 與知識工作流程，而不是只看產出速度。
article.author: OpenAI learning editor

paragraphs.en:
Organizations often plan capacity by counting the work that produces visible output: cases handled, reports written, tickets closed, or customers contacted. That approach is incomplete when quality depends on review. If a team can create work faster than it can verify it, the review queue becomes the real constraint.

This problem becomes more important with AI. Generative tools can produce drafts, classifications, summaries, and recommendations quickly. The first-stage productivity gain is easy to measure. However, if every output still needs a person to check facts, tone, compliance, or risk, total throughput may not improve. In some cases it can get worse because reviewers receive more items than they can process.

Capacity planning should therefore model both production and verification. Managers can start with a simple question: how many items can the team create, and how many can it safely review? If analysts can prepare one hundred cases a day but reviewers can approve only sixty, the sustainable capacity is not one hundred. The remaining forty become a queue, and the queue creates delay.

The next step is to distinguish review depth. Not every item needs the same level of attention. Low-risk outputs may require a quick sample check. Medium-risk work may need a standard checklist. High-risk cases may require full human approval. This risk-based design can protect quality without forcing the slowest review process onto every item.

Review quality also depends on concentration. A person who checks hundreds of nearly identical outputs may become less attentive over time. Capacity is therefore not only the number of minutes available. It also includes fatigue, context switching, and the difficulty of identifying rare but serious errors.

A useful dashboard can combine creation volume, review volume, queue size, average waiting time, rework rate, and serious-error rate. These measures show whether faster creation is actually improving the end-to-end process. They also reveal where additional staff, automation, or workflow redesign would have the greatest effect.

There is a management trade-off. Adding reviewers can increase capacity, but it may also add coordination cost. Automating review can reduce workload, but then the organization must validate the review system itself. Reducing review depth can speed up the process, but it may increase risk. The right answer depends on the cost of an error and how quickly problems can be detected and corrected.

The broader lesson is that capacity planning should follow the whole workflow, not only the step that produces the visible output. When technology accelerates one stage, managers should immediately ask where the bottleneck moves. A team is not truly faster if work is simply waiting in a different queue.

Scenario analysis can improve the plan. Suppose demand increases by 30 percent after a campaign. If creation capacity scales automatically but review remains fixed, queue growth can be forecast before launch. The team can temporarily reassign reviewers, tighten eligibility, or reduce nonessential checks for low-risk cases. This is better than discovering the constraint only after service levels deteriorate.

Sampling also deserves careful design. If only a fraction of low-risk outputs are reviewed, the sample should be large enough and selected in a way that can reveal systematic problems. Teams should avoid checking only convenient or easy cases. Stratified sampling by channel, customer type, model score, or error risk can provide better early warning.

Finally, managers should separate average capacity from peak capacity. A process that works on a normal Tuesday may fail at month-end, during a promotion, or after a system incident. Capacity plans should include buffers for predictable peaks and a clear escalation rule for unexpected surges. Review work is not an administrative detail; it is part of the production system.
paragraphs.zh: AI 讓產出端加速後，真正瓶頸很可能移到 review。Capacity planning 應同時衡量 creation volume、review volume、queue、waiting time、rework 與 serious errors，並依風險設計不同 review 深度。平均 capacity 與 peak capacity 也要分開，否則平日可行的流程可能在促銷、月底或事故期間失效。
paragraphs.ja: AIで生成速度が上がっても、レビュー能力が固定ならボトルネックは確認工程へ移ります。作成量だけでなく、レビュー量、待ち行列、手戻り、重大エラーを測り、リスクに応じてレビュー深度を変える必要があります。通常時とピーク時の能力も分けて考えることが重要です。
